sourceBody: Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.
Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.
Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.
An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.
Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.
The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.
A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.
Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.
List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.
Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.
Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.
A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.

agyRawDraftBody: Ṱhanga yaṋu i nga kona u kuvhanganya maḓi a mvula. Tshivhalo tsha maḓi tshi ḓitika nga roof area, rainfall na losses.
Tolani arali roof material yo tea u kuvhanganya maḓi a mvula musi ni sa athu u ṱumanya tank.
Shumisani roof area ine ya vhonala u bva nṱha na local rainfall records. Nga murahu ni dzhiele nzhele maḓi ane a pfula gutter, ane a vha diverted, kana ane a phulela nṱha ha tank yo ḓalaho.
Annual total a i ni vhudzi uri ndi maḓi mangana ane a ḓo vha hone nga tshifhinga tsha dry spell. Vhambedzani supply na mishumo ine na khou pulana.
Roof runoff i nga hwala buse, droppings na iṅwe contamination. First-flush diverter i thivhela maṅwe maḓi a first runoff uri a si dzhene kha tank.
Diversion ine ya ṱoḓea i ḓitika nga ṱhanga na system. Shumisani ndaela dza supplier dza sizing na maintenance; a hu na volume nthihi fhedzi ine ya shuma kha ṱhanga iṅwe na iṅwe.
Diverter a i iti uri maḓi o salaho a vhe o tsireledzea u nwiwa.
Tank size i ḓitika nga water demand, mvula, roof area na vhulapfu ha tshifhinga tsha dry periods.
Ṅwalani mutevhe wa mishumo yo lavhelelwaho nahone ni anganyele demand yayo u bva kha records dzaṋu vhaṋe. Vhambedzani zwenezwo na supply kha zwifhinga zwa ṅwaha (seasons).
Pulannani zwine na ḓo zwi ita musi maḓi o vhulungwaho a tshi thoma u vha maṱuku. Dzina ḽa province ḽoṱhe fhedzi a ḽi koni u ni vhudza tank size ine na i ṱoḓa.

Itani uri tank i dzule yo tibifhiwa, ni fute screen kha openings u thivhela zwikhokhonono (insects), nahone ni maintaine ṱhanga, gutters na diverter. Vhulungani maḓi a mvula kule na drinking-water pipes.
Maḓi ane a vhonala o kuna a nga kha ḓi vha e na germs kana chemicals. Vhudzisani local health authority nga ha testing na treatment yo teelaho mushumo wo lavhelelwaho.
Basic filter fhedzi a si drinking-water guarantee. Maḓi ane a shumiswa kha food crops na one a ṱoḓa safety assessment.

Keep tank covered, screen openings against insects, maintain roof/gutters/diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
